description.value: A tiny 2-site free camp on the Murtle River in the backcountry of Wells Gray Park; no confirmed amenities and hard access make this a spot only reached by determined wilderness travelers on foot or by canoe.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: OSM tags confirm a backcountry campsite (backcountry=yes, tents=yes, toilets=no, capacity=2, fee=no, openfire=yes) within Wells Gray Provincial Park. The BC Parks website confirms the park has backcountry areas with user-maintained campsites more than 1 km from roads, but never names Murtle River Camp specifically, so no site-level amenity details can be confirmed from website evidence. With toilets=no from OSM and no website corroboration for any optional amenities, nearly all amenity fields default to null.
concerns: Murtle River Camp is not mentioned by name anywhere on the BC Parks Wells Gray website; no site-level details can be confirmed from the website.
Capacity of 2 is very limited and the nature of that figure (tents vs. people) is unspecified.
Bicycle access to this backcountry site is unconfirmed; Wells Gray backcountry includes canoe-only and foot-access-only areas (e.g., Murtle Lake is canoe-only).
No address, phone, or email available for this listing.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Murtle River Camp is an extremely remote, primitive backcountry site (capacity 2, no toilets) with unconfirmed bicycle accessibility; it could suit bikepacking adventurers but there is insufficient evidence of road or trail access by bike, and the site offers no cyclist-specific infrastructure.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM tags provide the core facts: fee=no, openfire=yes, toilets=no, tents=yes, backcountry=yes, capacity=2. The BC Parks Wells Gray page confirms user-maintained backcountry campsites exist in the park but supplies no information specific to this node.

wow_evidence: tiny 2-site free camp on the Murtle River in the backcountry of Wells Gray Park; toilets=no
